reason: Follow the stem-cell lineage first, as the chapter suggests, before assembling mature bone.
expectation: The signals should guide some descendants toward bone-forming cells, though the intermediate stage is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework also seems useful, but the lineage comes first in the introduction.

effect: The lineage shows osteoblasts making matrix and some becoming embedded osteocytes; next I can assemble the mature bone framework.
reaction: The transition from matrix-producing to embedded cells is interesting, though the precursor terms are unexplained.
reason: Mineralize the collagen framework; it is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: Calcium phosphate crystals will strengthen the collagen framework, producing a mineralized bone structure.

effect: The framework now combines collagen's toughness with mineral's resistance to compression; it is ready for bone cells.
reaction: The contrast between flexible fibers and firmer mineral makes their roles clear.
reason: Add the bone cells to the mineralized framework; it is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: The cells will be shown within or around the framework as part of living bone, though the precise arrangement is uncertain.

effect: The cutaway places connected bone cells within the hard matrix; adding vessels is the next available step.
reaction: The tiny channels make living cells inside hard bone easier to picture.
reason: Add blood vessels to the bones; it is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: The vessels will supply the living bone tissue, though their exact arrangement is uncertain.

effect: Vessels supply nutrients through the channel network to embedded bone cells; the bones are ready for joint construction.
reaction: The distinction between blood cells remaining in vessels and nutrients reaching bone cells is helpful.
reason: Add cartilage to the living bones to begin forming the elbow joint; it is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: The cartilage will cap the bone ends at the elbow, providing smooth surfaces for movement.

effect: Cartilage now caps the facing elbow surfaces, showing how they slide against each other.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role easy to picture.
reason: Add the synovial capsule to continue building the joint; it is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: The capsule will enclose the joint surfaces with a small amount of fluid to support smooth movement.

effect: The capsule encloses the joint, and its lining supplies fluid that helps the cartilage-covered surfaces glide.
reaction: The connection between the lining and joint fluid clarifies the capsule’s role.
reason: Add the ligaments to support the elbow; this is the only gameplay option offered.
expectation: The ligaments will connect and stabilize the bones while allowing elbow movement.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported elbow, allowing bending while resisting sideways movement; the chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The contrasting arrows make the ligaments’ stabilizing role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mineralizing the collagen framework was most worthwhile: the planned inset and prose connect collagen’s toughness and mineral’s resistance to compression to bone structure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cells to the framework revisited their channels shortly after the lineage picture introduced them. It was useful, but felt somewhat repetitive.

surprise.text: The lineage showed some matrix-producing osteoblasts becoming embedded osteocytes, making bone seem more actively living than a simple mineral framework.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, though most were the only gameplay option offered. The mesodermal and mesenchymal precursor terms in the lineage were not explained.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: assembling living bone and then a joint made the relationship between structures and their functions engaging, even though the choices were mostly linear.
